{{nihongo|'''Hinomisaki Shrine'''|日御碕神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izumo Province]].

[[File:Hinomisaki-jinja Worship Hall of Hishizuminomiya (Shrine) 001.jpg|thumb|Hinomisaki-jinja Worship Hall of Hishizuminomiya (Shrine)<br/>Hinomisaki-jinja Worship Hall (Important Cultural Property)]][[File:Hinomisaki-jinja Worship Hall of kaminomiya (Shrine) 001.jpg|thumb|Kaminomiya (Kaminomiya)<br/>Worship Hall (Important Cultural Property)]]

'''Hinomisaki Shrine'' (Hinomisaki Shrine) is located in {{ill|Cape Hinomisaki|Q11505328|qid=Q11505328}} in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|qid=Q132751}}{{ill|Izumo, Shimane|Q825166|qid=Q825166}}. Commonly known as ``Misaki-san.'' He is revered as the ``Oyagami-sama'' of {{ill|Izumo-taisha|Q696362|qid=Q696362}}. Twelve shrine buildings and other buildings have been designated as national {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}.

==History==
Our company has two shrines, upper and lower. The upper shrine is called ``Kami no Miya,'' and the lower shrine is called ``Hishizuminomiya,'' and the two shrines are collectively called ``Hinosaki Shrine'' (''Hinosaki Daijingu Shrine''). In ancient times, Misaki Shrine is mentioned in ``{{ill|Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|qid=Q11395858}}'' and ``Misaki Shrine'' is mentioned in ``{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}{{Sfn|Shirai|1997|p=290}}, and the locals call it ``Misaki-san.''<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.izumo.shimane.jp/www/contents/1260146321415/files/p16-17.pdf |title=Public Relations Izumo No. 114 |access-date=2022-07-27 |publisher=Izumo City |format=PDF}}</ref>.According to the shrine's legend, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Suenarison}}, after the nation-building of {{ill|Izumo|Q11395836|qid=Q11395836}}, became Kumanarimine<ref group="note">currently Mt. Tengu. It is located on the border between Yakumo Village, Yatsuka District, Shimane Prefecture, and Hirose Town, Nogi District, and was once called Mt. Kumanu.In the Izumo Fudoki, it is described as ``Kumano Mountain.The so-called shrine seat of Kumano Okami.''Near the top of the mountain, there is a huge rock where Kumano Okami was enshrined in the former shrine of {{ill|Kumano Taisha|Q11568887|qid=Q11568887}}. </ref>, looking for a place to rest, he read the oak leaves with the wind and came to a stop on the hill behind the <ref group="note">Himisaki Shrine/Kamimiya Shrine</ref>. It is said that his son, {{ill|Ame-no-Fuyukinu|Q48744862|qid=Q48744862|lt=Amanzukine no Mikoto}}, enshrined his soul there, and Kakuregaoka ({{ill|Kofun|Q1141225|qid=Q1141225}}) is currently located behind the main shrine building.{{Sfn|Shirai|1997|p=290}}. Sunset Shrine was originally enshrined in Fukushima (currently {{ill|Fumi-shima|Q5508550|qid=Q5508550}}), and when Amazukine no Mikoto was in Fukushima, {{jalink|Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602} } is said to have descended and was enshrined with a divine edict that said, ``I will bless the people of the world, so please worship me quickly.''{{Sfn|Shirai|1997|p=290}}<ref name=":0" /> is a holy place for ascetic training and is described as a ``holy address'' in ``{{ill|Ryōjin Hishō|Q3010584|qid=Q3010584}}'' compiled by {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|Q317984|qid=Q317984|lt=Retired Emperor Goshirakawa}} at the end of the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}. The Shrine of the Gods (Kami no Miya) was currently enshrined on Kakuregaoka Hill behind the main shrine, but in the 13th year of Emperor An'ei ({{ill|6th century BC|Q25296|qid=Q25296|lt=536 BC}}), it was moved to its current location by imperial order, and Nishingu Shrine (Lower Palace) It is said that it was enshrined on {{ill|Fumi-shima|Q5508550|qid=Q5508550|lt=Keijima (Hikijima)}}, but was moved to its current location in {{ill|Tenryaku|Q1346281|qid=Q1346281}}2 (948) by imperial order of Emperor Murakami.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />.

Since ancient times, it has been highly revered by the {{ill|Imperial Court of Japan|Q30253177|qid=Q30253177|lt=Imperial Court}}, and since the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}, it has been revered by the {{ill|Shogunate|Q1074150|qid=Q1074150}}, and the shrine has been renovated. {{ill|Izumo Province|Q582846|qid=Q582846}}{{ill|Matsue Domain|Q1017072|qid=Q1017072}}'s first generation, {{ill|Horio Tadauji|Q3140540|qid=Q3140540}}, gave a shrine territory of over 780 koku, and the Tokugawa shogunate also gave 600 koku {{Sfn|Shirai|1997|p=290}}. It is said to be the successor shrine to Izumo Taisha in the Sanin region {{Sfn|Great Dictionary of Shinto|1969|p=200}}.The current shrine building of Nissu Shrine, God's Palace, was built by the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ar|شوغونية توكوغاوا|ast|Shogunato Tokugawa|az|Tokuqava şoqunluğu|azb|توکوقاوا سولا‌له‌سی|ba|Токугава сёгунаты|bcl|Shogunato kan Tokugawa|be|Сёгунат Такугава|bg|Шогунат Токугава|bs|Tokugawa|ca|Shogunat Tokugawa|ckb|زنجیرە شۆگنی تۆکوگاوا|cs|Šógunát Tokugawa|da|Tokugawa-shogunatet|de|Tokugawa-Shōgunat|el|Σογκουνάτο Τοκουγκάβα|eo|Tokugava ŝogunlando|es|Shogunato Tokugawa|et|Tokugawa šogunaat|eu|Tokugawa shogunerria|fa|شوگون‌سالاری توکوگاوا|fi|Tokugawa-shōgunaatti|fr|Shogunat Tokugawa|gl|Shogunato Tokugawa|hak|Edo mok-fú|he|שוגונות טוקוגאווה|hi|तोकुगावा शोगुनराज|hr|Šogunat Tokugawa|hu|Edo-bakufu|ia|Shogunato Tokugawa|id|Keshogunan Tokugawa|is|Tokugawa-veldið|it|Shogunato Tokugawa|ja|江戸幕府|jv|Keshogunan Tokugawa|ka|ტოკუგავა|ko|에도 막부|la|Tokugawa Bakufu|lt|Tokugavos šiogūnatas|lv|Tokugavas sjogunāts|ms|Kesyogunan Tokugawa|nl|Tokugawa-shogunaat|no|Tokugawa-shōgunatet|or|ତୋକୁଗାୱା ଶୋଗୁନେତ|pa|ਤੋਕੂਗਾਵਾ ਸ਼ੋਗੁਨ|pl|Siogunat Tokugawów|pnb|توکوگاوا شوگون شاہی|pt|Xogunato Tokugawa|ro|Shogunatul Tokugawa|ru|Сёгунат Токугава|sco|Tokugawa shogunate|sh|Šogunat Tokugawa|simple|Tokugawa shogunate|sl|Šogunat Tokugava|sq|Shogunati Tokugava|sr|Шогунат Токугава|su|Kashogunan Tokugawa|sv|Tokugawa|th|รัฐบาลเอโดะ|tl|Shogunatong Tokugawa|tr|Tokugawa şogunluğu|tt|Tokugawa sögunatı|uk|Сьоґунат Едо|ur|توکوگاوا شوگون شاہی|uz|Tokugava|vi|Mạc phủ Tokugawa|wuu|江户幕府|zh|江户幕府|zh_classical|江戶幕府|zh_min_nan|Edo bō͘-hú|zh_yue|江戶幕府|qid=Q205662}}3rd generation {{ill|jiangjun|ja|将軍|ko|장군 (고려)|mn|Жанжин|zh|將軍 (東亞古代)|zh_yue|將軍 (中國古代)|qid=Q15903946}} and {{jalink|virtue}. Since then, it has been revered by successive feudal lords {{Sfn|Great Dictionary of Shinto|1969|p=200}}. Both shrines are in Gongen style modeled after Nikko Toshogu Shrine<ref name=":1" />. The sculptures of three monkeys and a dragon are also identical to those of Nikko Toshogu Shrine.

{{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}In 4, he was ranked as Kokuheishosha.

The name ``Sunset Shrine'' originates from the fact that, while {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}} was built to ``protect the day of the book of the day,'' Hinomisaki Shrine received an ``imperial command'' to ``protect the night of the book of the day.''<ref>It was installed locally, according to the history board of Hinosaki Shrine. </ref>.

Twelve shrine buildings, including Nissu Shrine, Shrine of the Gods, Romon, Corridor, Purification Place, Treasure House, and Monkyakujinsha, as well as two {{ill|Torii|Q234731|qid=Q234731}} and five stone {{ill|Stone lantern|ar|فانوس حجري|ast|Tōrō|az|Toro (fənər)|be|Таро (ліхтар)|es|Tōrō|fa|تورو|fi|Tōrō|fr|Tōrō|hi|तोरो|id|Tōrō|ja|灯籠|ko|등롱|nl|Tōrō|oc|Toro (lantèrna)|pt|Tōrō|ru|Торо (фонарь)|sl|Kamnite svetilke|sv|Ishidoro|vi|Đèn đá|zh|燈籠 (建築裝飾)|qid=Q12012294|lt=lantern}}, have been designated as important cultural properties of the country.

* Sunset Palace (Lower Palace): (Important Cultural Property)
*: It is said that ``Hyakki Shrine'', which had been enshrined on Keijima (Hikijima) in front of Kiyoe Beach, just outside the shrine grounds, was moved to its current location in 948 by an order of Emperor Murakami. The interior is divided into an upper and a lower tier, and according to ancient documents, the upper tier is said to have been called the ``Kagura-sho'' <ref name=":0" />.

** Seiden
** Worship Hall
** Tamagaki

* Temple of God (Upper Shrine): (Important Monument)
*: It was originally enshrined on the hill behind the current shrine building, but it is said to have been moved to its current location in the 13th year of Emperor An'ei<ref name=":0" />.

; crafts
:* White armor with helmet and large sleeves 1 territory - Designated March 31, 1953<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/401 |title=White armor (with helmet and large sleeves) / National treasure/Important cultural property (work of art) |access-date=2022-07-27 |publisher=Nationally designated cultural property database}}</ref>.::: Made in the Kamakura period. Body height: 63.6{{ill|Centimetre|Q174728|qid=Q174728}}, helmet height: 11.2cm, sleeve height: 39.4cm<ref name=":3" />. During the Edo period, it was known as {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|qid=Q242800}} votive armor. At the end of the Edo period, the temple suffered severe damage such as its doshiito, and in 1805, by order of Harusato Matsudaira, the lord of the Matsue domain, it was repaired in Edo to its current form without damaging its original appearance. At that time, Shirokawa dyed with the words ``Bunka Ninen Repair'' was used to repair the damaged parts, and the remaining items such as the threads and cords that were removed are kept. Ataka Teramoto, who was in charge of the repairs, has written a 61-point repair record, ``Annotations for repairing the armor of Lord Minamoto no Yoritomo.'' |publisher=Tokyo National Museum}}</ref>. {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ar|متحف طوكيو الوطني|arz|متحف طوكيو الوطنى|ast|Muséu Nacional de Tokiu|az|Tokio Milli Muzeyi|ba|Токио милли музейы|be|Такійскі нацыянальны музей|bg|Токийски национален музей|ca|Museu Nacional de Tòquio|cs|Národní muzeum v Tokiu|de|Nationalmuseum Tokio|eo|Tokia Nacia Muzeo|es|Museo Nacional de Tokio|et|Tokyo Rahvusmuuseum|eu|Tokioko Museo Nazionala|fa|موزه ملی توکیو|fi|Tokion kansallismuseo|fr|Musée national de Tokyo|gl|Museo Nacional de Tokyo|he|המוזיאון הלאומי של טוקיו|hr|Nacionalni muzej u Tokiju|hu|Tokiói Nemzeti Múzeum|hy|Տոկիոյի ազգային թանգարան|id|Museum Nasional Tokyo|it|Museo nazionale di Tokyo|ja|東京国立博物館|jv|Musiyum Nasiyonal Tokyo|ka|ტოკიოს ეროვნული მუზეუმი|ko|도쿄 국립박물관|mk|Токиски национален музеј|ml|ടോക്കിയോ നാഷണൽ മ്യൂസിയം|ms|Muzium Negara Tokyo|mzn|توکیو ملی موزه|nl|Nationaal museum van Tokio|no|Tokyos nasjonalmuseum|pa|ਟੋਕੀਓ ਰਾਸ਼ਟਰੀ ਅਜਾਇਬ ਘਰ|pl|Muzeum Narodowe w Tokio|pnb|ٹوکیو قومی عجائب گھر|pt|Museu Nacional de Tóquio|ru|Токийский национальный музей|simple|Tokyo National Museum|sl|Tokijski narodni muzej|sr|Nacionalni muzej u Tokiju|ta|டோக்கியோ தேசிய அருங்காட்சியகம்|th|พิพิธภัณฑสถานแห่งชาติโตเกียว|tr|Tokyo Ulusal Müzesi|tt|Токио дәүләт музее|uk|Токійський національний музей|vi|Bảo tàng Quốc gia Tokyo|zh|东京国立博物馆|zh_yue|東京國立博物館|qid=Q653433}} deposited ({{ill|En'ya Takasada|Q11428604|qid=Q11428604}} donation).

== National Natural Monument ==
[[File:Hinomisaki-jinja Fumi-Shima-jinja in Fumi Island 001.jpg|thumb|Kyojima. There is Tsunejima Shrine, a shrine outside the precincts, and the former enshrinement site of Nishingu Shrine (Shimonomiya)]]
* {{ill|Fumi-shima|Q5508550|qid=Q5508550}} Black-tailed black-tailed gull breeding ground - Designated on March 8, 1922 (Taisho 11)<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2151 |title=Keijima black-tailed black-tailed black-tailed breeding ground / Historic site, scenic beauty, and natural monument |access-date=2022-07-27 |publisher=Nationally designated cultural properties database / Agency for Cultural Affairs}}</ref>.
:: Tsunejima Island owned by Hinomisaki Shrine and the former resting place of Sunset Shrine (Shinonomiya) (managed by Izumo City). {{ill|Sea of Japan|Q27092|qid=Q27092}}A typical {{ill|Black-tailed gull|Q623194|qid=Q623194}} breeding ground in the western part of the country.

* Ono family residence/{{ill|nagayamon|Q11651929|qid=Q11651929}}: The Ono family of Hinomisaki Shrine {{ill|Shake (social class)|Q11588367|qid=Q11588367}} was the home of {{ill|Izumo-taisha|Q696362|qid=Q696362}} before the war. link|Izumo Kunizo|Q11395856|Senke/Kitajima}} and {{ill|Iwami Province|Q1053709|qid=Q1053709|lt=Iwami}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379|lt=Ichinomiya}} {{ill|Mononobe Shrine (Oda)|Q11570699|qid=Q11570699|lt=Mononobe Shrine}} ({{ill|Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|qid=Q132751}}{{ill|Ōda, Shimane|Q384796|qid=Q384796}})・The Kaneko Family Shrine '', and had the status of being ranked as one of the 14 Shake families nationwide ({{ill|Baron|Q165503|qid=Q165503}}).* Underwater ruins: From Keijima to Kuroshima, there are man-made underwater caves and approaches and shrines with remains of man-made gravel. Similar underwater ruins also exist in Hinomisaki<ref>{{PDF|[https://web.archive.org/web/20041109045828/http://www.world-ss.co.jp/R-Gijyutu/KaityuuIseki/teiansyo.pdf Hinomisaki Undersea Ruins Survey]}} ({{ill|Internet Archive|Q461|qid=Q461|lt=Archive}} as of November 9, 2004)</ref>.
